title: Squares of a Sorted Array
prompt:
Write a function in `solution.ts` that returns an array of the squares of each number from a sorted input array, also in sorted order.

**Approach -- Two Pointers from Both Ends:**
Since the input is sorted (may contain negatives), the largest squares are at the extremes. Use a `left` pointer at index 0 and a `right` pointer at the last index. Compare `Math.abs(nums[left])` and `Math.abs(nums[right])`; place the larger square at the end of the result array and move that pointer inward. Use a `while` loop that continues while `left <= right`.

**Requirements:**
1. `export function sortedSquares(nums: number[]): number[]` -- takes a sorted array of integers and returns a new array of their squares in non-decreasing order
2. Use a `while` loop with two pointers converging from both ends
3. Build the result array from right to left (largest to smallest)

**Examples:**
```typescript
sortedSquares([-4, -1, 0, 3, 10]); // [0, 1, 9, 16, 100]
sortedSquares([-7, -3, 2, 3, 11]); // [4, 9, 9, 49, 121]
sortedSquares([1]);                 // [1]
```

**Complexity:**
- Time: O(n) -- single pass with two pointers
- Space: O(n) -- result array of the same length
hints: The largest squared value must come from either the leftmost or rightmost element
Use Math.abs() to compare magnitudes of the two ends
Fill the result array from the back (index n-1) toward the front
Move the pointer whose absolute value was larger inward after placing its square

solution.ts.name: sortedSquares
solution.ts.description: Export sortedSquares as a named export
Use a while loop for the two-pointer traversal
